summary: This edition makes 3 reader-facing changes: 2 additions, 1 correction. No guidance was removed.

items.section: Section 17. LLM observability as a first-class discipline
items.title: Separate monitor coverage and review delay
items.whatChanged: Report monitor coverage, time to automated review, time to human review and escalation rate separately. An action being logged does not establish timely review, and a low flag rate does not establish good detection. State which platforms and tool paths the denominator includes.
items.why: The existing paragraph inventories surfaces and responder availability but does not separate these operational measures.

sources.title: Measurements for understanding the pace of AI development inside frontier labs

items.section: Section 16. Evals as the release contract
items.title: Compare safety evaluations with production decisions
items.whatChanged: Check whether safety-evaluation behavior transfers to comparable production decisions. Match cases on the context before the decision, keep grading definitions aligned and report the remaining case-mixture differences. Where task framing may matter, compare an unchanged task with controlled descriptions of the evaluation objective. Do not assume that evaluation awareness always inflates safety scores.
items.why: The November 3 study supports testing objective framing and the direction of transfer, absent from the current generic production-monitoring layer.

sources.title: Eval-production behavior gaps in agent safety and the role of eval-awareness

items.title: Record the current evidence review
items.whatChanged: Updated the evidence-review date and limited current-access assertions to sources reopened in this prepared run.
items.why: Readers can distinguish the common cutoff from the date on which primary evidence was checked.
